name: Apong (Rice Beer)
ingredients: Sticky rice or local red rice
Starter culture (Opo/Epe - a mix of local wild herbs and rice flour)
instructions: 1. Steam the rice until it is cooked but slightly firm.
2. Spread the rice on a mat to cool completely.
3. Grind the traditional 'Opo' starter cake into a fine powder and mix it thoroughly with the cooled rice.
4. Transfer the mixture into a clean bamboo vessel or earthen pot lined with banana leaves.
5. Seal the container tightly to prevent air entry and store it in a cool, dark place for 3 to 7 days depending on the desired strength and sweetness.
6. Once fermentation is complete, dilute the concentrate with water, strain the liquid, and serve it fresh.
description: Apong is an integral part of the socio-cultural fabric of tribes in Arunachal Pradesh, such as the Adi, Nyishi, and Apatani. It is considered a sacred drink served during festivals, marriages, and community gatherings, symbolizing hospitality and friendship.
